consumer: The find-item quest's possession gate (a dialogue/condition u_has_items check) asking 'does the character have item flashlight?' and computing a yes/no from it
scope: only the character's own carried items, searched recursively as the predicate does (including items nested inside worn/held containers)
decisive_source: src/condition.cpp::conditional_t<T>::set_has_items builds the gate lambda returning actor->has_charges(item_id,count) || actor->has_amount(item_id,count) over the alpha/beta player actor — an engine-COMPUTED boolean, not raw state
divergence: A flashlight nested inside a worn backpack: the engine predicate (has_amount, which recurses via visit_items per visitable.cpp::visit_internal) returns true, but a reader of the flat avatar.carried_items[] snapshot (arcopolis_export.cpp::write_carried_items, which only emits top-level wielded/worn/inventory items and never recurses into container contents) returns false — exposing a raw-state (S) answer as wrong against the C predicate
